clue.text: Bugs sailor wearing marks of injury

indicators.note: the scars are worn around the sailor, so they enclose him

parts.note: scars are the marks an injury leaves
AB, able seaman, is the crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An insect-ridden sailor covered in old wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarabs are beetles, and bugs is used loosely for any insects.

clue.text: May must accept European sovereignty, being blue

indicators.note: the may word takes in the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: may and can both express permission
rule is sovereign power

explanation.surface: A prime minister called May must accept European rule and is downcast for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' reads as Theresa May the politician; it is the verb meaning can.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky colour, a shade of blue.

clue.text: Servant once needing line for new merchant

indicators.note: needing says the servant word must take on a change
line for new means line replaces new

parts.note: a retainer was a servant of a noble household in former times

explanation.surface: An old-time servant needs a fresh line of work as a trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a seller of goods to the public, a merchant.

clue.text: Succeed, seeing bishop cut connection across Italy

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the hang-up phrase stretches across Italy, holding it inside

parts.note: to ring off is to end a phone call
IT is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: A bishop hangs up on a call to Italy and somehow it works out.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring it off is an idiom for managing to achieve something difficult.

clue.text: Dress for the south of France?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dress of calf length
second meaning: the French name for the southern region of France

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an outfit chosen for the Riviera; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a mid-calf skirt or dress, and le Midi is the region of southern France.

clue.text: Out when bound to be heard

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: to be heard says the word is spelt as it sounds, not as written

parts.note: a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Absent at the very moment one is obliged to testify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be heard' looks like 'certain to be heard'; bound is the jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean unconscious or sleeping, as in out like a light.

clue.text: Source of marijuana in nick gets support

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the nick word

parts.note: to nick someone is British slang for arresting them

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Cannabis found in a police station earns someone backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang both for a police station and for arresting someone; here it is the arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is a part of a chair that supports the arm.

clue.text: Experience involved pies and poetry

indicators.note: involved means intricate, tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: An event that included pies and verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or experience in someone's life.

clue.text: Place for taking off sports kit after broadcast

indicators.note: the kit comes after the broadcast word in the answer

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a team's strip is its sports kit

explanation.surface: Somewhere to change out of your football gear once the match has been televised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests undressing next to 'sports kit', but it is an aircraft's take-off; a strip is a team's matching kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft leave the ground.

clue.text: Dietary necessity for one in ten

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: the numeral one is placed inside the word ten

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something one in ten people needs to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is an essential nutrient the body must get from food.

clue.text: Degree of penalty skills?

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty
arts are skills, as in the arts of persuasion

explanation.surface: How good a footballer is at taking penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penalty skills' suggests spot-kicks; it splits into a fine and arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine arts is a university course, so one can hold a degree in it; the clue's question mark flags this stretch.

clue.text: CIA fury unleashed — concealing personal documents held in trust

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hide the documents within them
unleashed means let loose, so the letters run wild

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: The CIA's anger erupts and it hides the private papers it was given to keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiduciary arrangement involves property managed on behalf of others, so held in trust.

clue.text: Craft prone to break surface roughly

indicators.note: the lying word breaks into the jumbled letters, sitting inside them
roughly says the letters of surface are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
lying flat is being prone

explanation.surface: A boat liable to break the water's surface in rough seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat beside 'surface'; it is any vehicle, here one from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying saucer is a supposed alien spacecraft, so a craft in the vehicle sense.

clue.text: Popular girl's set out of sorts

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Di is a girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS
to pose a question is to set it

explanation.surface: A popular girl's group of friends is feeling a bit off.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed means slightly unwell, which is what out of sorts means.

clue.text: Spirits depressing Conservative voter's tale

indicators.note: in a down clue the spirits sit on top of, pressing down on, the voter

parts.note: shorts are small measures of spirits
a Tory supports Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Drinks bring down a Tory voter's story.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a short is a single measure of spirits such as whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story is a brief work of prose fiction, a tale.

clue.text: See 22
Support police crossing river for basic foodstuffs

parts.note: to root for a team is to support it

indicators.note: the police word crosses over the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: cops are police
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Backing the police as they ford a river for supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Root crops such as potatoes and turnips are staple vegetables.

clue.text: Answer could be a blend of liquids, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the answer to a problem
second meaning: a mixture with one substance dissolved in a liquid

explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry the word is a substance dissolved in a liquid; 'perhaps' admits a blend is only loosely that.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the resolution of a puzzle and a dissolved mixture.

clue.text: Sort of title here rewritten in pen

indicators.note: the rewritten letters go inside the pen word

parts.note: a fold is a pen for sheep

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of here are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A property deed redrafted here in ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests writing; it is a sheep enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold is a form of land title giving outright ownership.

clue.text: Witty words from English farm animals

parts.note: a pig and a ram, side by side

explanation.surface: Clever remarks drawn from English livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short clever saying, a pithy witticism.

clue.text: Cruising, having accepted new ideas?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: aboard a ship on a cruise
second meaning: in agreement, having signed up to a plan

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means physically on a ship and also figuratively signed up to a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a voyage are on deck, and colleagues who have embraced a plan are said to be on side the same way.

clue.text: Plant producing fine bread regularly?

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of bread

parts.note: the second and fourth letters are taken

explanation.surface: A plant that yields good bread now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a flowering plant grown for its edible green pods.

clue.text: Changing tack on a perfect sweet

indicators.note: changing tells us to reorder these letters

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Switching sailing course towards a perfect sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pontefract cake is a small round British liquorice sweet from the Yorkshire town of Pontefract.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquorice disc is a confection, which is what a sweet means in British English.

clue.text: Clever us, never set up to reveal guarantee

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
reveal says the letters are on show inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smug boast that we are never clever, put on show as a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'reveal guarantee' as the definition, but 'reveal' is the signal that the letters lie inside the clue's words; the definition is 'guarantee' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, to guarantee it.

clue.text: See 12
Polish a line for the appendix?

parts.note: gloss is a shine or polish
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: Buffing up a line of text for the back of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with a capital looks like the nationality; it is the verb or noun for shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms often placed at the back of a book, as an appendix is.

clue.text: Some hear a shark, disregarding danger

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people hear about a shark and take no notice of the threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means reckless, acting without thought for the risk.

clue.text: Joint scheme needing to employ one high flier

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint, as in co-owner

indicators.note: the scheme takes on the one, holding it inside

parts.note: a plot is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shared plan that needs to hire one high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' suggests a star employee; here it is literal, someone who flies a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A copilot is the second pilot of an aircraft, so literally someone who flies high.

clue.text: Make snap changes?

parts.note: snap means a photograph, not sudden; the changes are retouching a photo

explanation.walkthrough: Snap changes sound like hasty decisions, but a snap is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush is to retouch a photograph, altering its image with a fine spray or software.

clue.text: Many ultimately in prison die horribly — from this?

definitions.text: Many ultimately in prison die horribly — from this?

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the prison word

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of many

parts.note: its last letter is taken

indicators.note: horribly says the letters of die are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a poison is why so many prisoners end up dying horribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a deadly poison, historically used in executions, so the whole clue describes it.
